title: Harden TampinesSteamArray::correct_thermo() against out-of-range (p,h) panics
description:
TampinesSteamArray::correct_thermo() (crates/tampines-steam-tables/src/openfoam_algorithms/rhoPimpleFoam/mod.rs, from op-21g.10) calls t_ph_eqm/v_ph_eqm/kappa_t_ph_eqm/mu_ph_eqm/lambda_ph_eqm/cp_ph_eqm directly per cell -- these PANIC (not Result) if (p,h) falls out of the valid IAPWS-IF97 range (e.g. below 273.15K), unlike OPCPFluidArray::correct_thermo() (outram-park-fork-coolprop), which does 'if let Ok(state) = flash::state_ph(...) { update } else { keep previous rho/T/psi for this cell }' -- a graceful degradation, not a panic, if a cell wanders out of range mid-simulation.

Fix direction (not yet decided/implemented): either (a) wrap the tampines-steam-tables (p,h) flash calls in a fallible variant if one exists or can be added, matching CoolProp's graceful-degradation pattern, or (b) some other guard against out-of-range panics during a running PIMPLE loop.

User explicitly deferred this (2026-07-13) -- wants to check the situation manually first before any fix is attempted. Do not implement without further discussion.
closed_reason: Decided against: user (2026-07-14) wants panic-on-out-of-range, not graceful degradation like OPCPFluidArray -- a stale-state fallback would silently produce a nonphysical cell state during a running PIMPLE loop, which is worse than a loud crash. Verified there is nothing to change: t_ph_eqm/v_ph_eqm/kappa_t_ph_eqm/mu_ph_eqm/lambda_ph_eqm/cp_ph_eqm already return plain uom values (no Result to unwrap) and already panic!() deep in ph_flash_region -> check_if_within_ph_validity_region on out-of-range (p,h). correct_thermo() as committed in 356daff already has the desired behavior.

title: TampinesSteamArray::step() pressure oscillation with nonzero inlet velocity BC
description: Discovered 2026-07-14 while building set_inlet_velocity/set_inlet_enthalpy/set_outlet_pressure BC setters for TampinesSteamArray (lateral_coupling.rs), in service of wiring TampinesSteamArray into fhr_sim_v2's steam generator tube. First real exercise anywhere in the crate of step()'s pressure-velocity (PISO) coupling under a nonzero Dirichlet velocity BC -- every prior test uses default zero-gradient/passive BCs or drives he alone via set_temperature_vector. Reproduction: 10-cell, 1m pipe, 1e-4 m^2 area, dt=5e-5s (acoustically stable per dx/c_sound), pre-conditioned near 370K/1bar, then inlet velocity=0.5 m/s + inlet enthalpy=4.2e5 J/kg + outlet pressure=1e5 Pa fixed. Pressure develops a large non-physical oscillation within ~10 steps (ranging ~1e5 to ~9e5 Pa across cells against a fixed 1e5 Pa outlet BC and modest inflow -- nothing in the setup should drive a 9x pressure excursion) and panics out of the valid IAPWS-IF97 range by step ~27 (see ph_flash_eqm check_if_within_ph_validity_region). Kept as an #[ignore]d regression test: openfoam_algorithms::rhoPimpleFoam::lateral_coupling::tests::inlet_outlet_bcs_drive_flow_and_outlet_pressure_settles_near_imposed_value. Suspect the source_p boundary-flux special case for BoundaryCondition::FixedValue velocity (mod.rs step(), the 'match self.u.boundary[pi].bc' block) but not confirmed -- root-causing the PISO instability was out of scope for that session. Blocks: op-21g.6 (multiphase suite work that might build on this) is unaffected, but any consumer wanting to drive TampinesSteamArray as a prescribed-BC pipe (e.g. tampines fhr_sim_v2's steam generator tube) is blocked until this is fixed.

notes.content:
2026-07-14 follow-up: root-caused and fixed one real bug (phi_hbya boundary write-back missing for FixedValue velocity patches in mod.rs step() -- self.phi kept HbyA's always-zero-gradient boundary extrapolation instead of the corrected flux used in the pressure source, corrupting the next step's rhoEqn continuity). Also added the user-requested SIMPLE/PISO/PIMPLE infrastructure: get/set_n_outer_correctors, get/set_n_inner_correctors, get/set_pressure_under_relaxation, get/set_velocity_under_relaxation, and set_piso_algorithm/set_simple_algorithm/set_pimple_algorithm presets (mod.rs). With SIMPLE + heavy under-relaxation (alpha_p=0.02, alpha_u=0.3) and staying well clear of the saturation boundary, the pressure oscillation is much better behaved (bounded ~25% swing surviving 40+ iterations, vs a 9x blowup crashing by iteration 27 before the fix) but NOT fully resolved -- temperature still drifts upward and eventually exceeds the 1073.15K validity ceiling; the energy equation's stability under residual pressure noise was not root-caused. Separately (not the same run, found by moving inlet enthalpy near h_f at 1 bar): correct_thermo's (p,h) region classification and thermal_conductivity's internal (T,p) re-classification can disagree right at the saturation boundary, hitting pt_flash_eqm::cp_tp_eqm_single_phase's FwdEqnRegion::Region4 => todo!() panic -- this would block real steam-generator (boiling) use regardless of the pressure-oscillation outcome. All three findings documented in the (still #[ignore]d) regression test inlet_outlet_bcs_drive_flow_and_outlet_pressure_settles_near_imposed_value's doc comment. Net: real progress, but wiring TampinesSteamArray into a driven steam-generator-tube use case (e.g. fhr_sim_v2) remains blocked on findings 2 and 3.
2026-07-14: FINDING 3 (saturation-boundary todo!()) RESOLVED. lambda_ph_eqm's critical-enhancement term (thermal_conductivity::lambda_2_crit_enhancement_term_tp_two_phase_estimate) delegated cp/cv/kappa_t to single-phase (T,p) routines that todo!() in region 4 (T,p not independent on the saturation line). lambda_ph_eqm calls this for EVERY region (x=0 region1, x=1 region2/3, interior region4), so the fix branches: single-phase (x==0 or x==1) keeps the exact (t,p) single-phase values bit-for-bit (verified: the 53 single-phase steam-table lambda tests that a naive t_sat-everywhere version broke now all pass again); genuine two-phase (0<x<1) quality-weights the saturated region-1/region-2 values at t_sat, mirroring cp_ph_eqm's own region-4 handling. Two new verification tests (both pass): thermal_conductivity::tests::lambda_ph_two_phase_is_finite_and_bracketed (finite, positive, bracketed by sat vapour..liquid, monotonic in quality at 1 bar) and openfoam_algorithms::rhoPimpleFoam::tests::correct_thermo_survives_two_phase_boiling_cell (a TampinesSteamArray cell at 1 bar / h=1.5MJ/kg / x~0.48 survives correct_thermo, T~T_sat, all fields finite). Full suite 909 passed / 0 failed. This unblocks a boiling steam-generator-tube model. Remaining on this bead: the PISO/stiff-liquid pressure-oscillation robustness (findings 1-2) for driving TampinesSteamArray hard; the source-clobber root cause (separate) is already fixed + pushed in 540fd45.
2026-07-14: TampinesSteamArray WIRED into fhr_sim_v2's steam-generator tube (secondary_loop/mod.rs), replacing the lumped h_out=h_in+Q/mdot energy balance with the spatially-resolved (p,h) steam-table physics. Persistent array (build_steam_generator_tube), driven 25 acoustic-CFL substeps per TH step, outlet enthalpy read back to feed the turbine. New standalone validation test steam_generator_tube_boils_feedwater (feedwater 80degC -> boiling at 2 bar, x crosses 0 at step 5416, passes). Two integration bugs found + fixed (see tampines-steam-tables/docs/notes.md 'Correction log'): (1) default pressure floor was sat_pressure_4(273.15) EXACTLY -> clamped cells land on saturation line -> (p,h) validity guard's exact-equality Region-4 test todo!()-panics; fixed by nudging floor *1.001 into Region 1; (2) pre-init pressure (2 bar) mismatched operating outlet BC (1.2 bar) -> depressurisation rarefaction cooled a cell below 273.15K; fixed by matching pre-init to operating pressure. title: TampinesSteamArray energy over-cooling under fast flashing (Edwards blowdown plateau under-predicted)
description:
The Edwards-O'Brien blowdown V&V test (tests/edwards_blowdown.rs) exposes an energy-conservation limitation in TampinesSteamArray::step(). During the violent subcooled->two-phase decompression the h-form energy equation loses ~10x more enthalpy than the reversible dh=dp/rho, so the bulk liquid drops to subcooled and only flashes near ambient instead of holding the ~350-380 psia (p_sat at T0~505K) flashing plateau. Measured GS-1 plateau ~17 psia vs experimental ~350-367 psia; GS-1 pressure RMSE vs digitised Data ~276 psia.

Root cause: step() runs the explicit rhoEqn continuity rho = rho_old - dt*div(phi), but correct_thermo then OVERWRITES rho with the EOS (p,h) density each inner correction. That breaks the discrete cancellation of the h*div(phi) term in d(rho h)/dt + div(phi h) = dp/dt, so enthalpy is not conserved through a fast density change. Reducing dt (30us->10us) does not fix the ratio; it is structural.

NOTE: this is the ACCURACY limitation only. The STABILITY question Ethan raised (explicit scheme cools empty pipe to ~1C and pressure rebounds past 0.42s) is CURED by our PIMPLE array: past 0.42s min T=358K, tail pressure rebound +0.9 psia, void stable 0.997 -- no artefact. See test doc comment for full V&V write-up.

Possible fixes to evaluate (need own V&V): (a) conservative (rho*e or rho*h) energy update using the continuity-consistent density rather than the EOS density in the ddt term; (b) an internal-energy (e) formulation; (c) sub-cycling the flash within the corrector. Do NOT loosen the test tolerance -- assertions there are sanity-only by design.

notes.content: RESOLVED 2026-07-16. Fixed with two coupled thermodynamic corrections (no clamps): (1) conservative energy ddt using the CONTINUITY density rho_cont = rho_old - dt*div(phi) rebuilt from the final mass flux (new fvm::ddt_coeff_old), so (rho_cont-rho_old)/dt = -div(phi) exactly and the h*div(phi) term cancels term-for-term against div(phi h), restoring rho Dh/Dt = dp/dt -- this is approach (a) from the bead; (2) pressure-eqn compressibility psi = d(rho)/dp|_h (central finite-diff of the (p,h) flash at fixed enthalpy) replacing the frozen quality-weighted isothermal rho*kappa_T, which was ~100x too small in the two-phase dome and let the pressure overshoot through the plateau. Results: GS-1 flashing plateau 17 -> 393 psia (target ~350-367); RMSE vs Data 276 -> 60 psia; stable full 600 ms; no non-physical subcooling (void grows gradually, fluid holds near p_sat). All 915 lib tests still green. See collaboration/edwards_tampines_regen/debug_log.md and tests/edwards_blowdown.rs doc comment. Residual: plateau ~8% high + shallow late decline (HEM-closure accuracy, separate from the missing-plateau failure).

Hybrid all-Mach (rhoCentralFoam + rhoPimpleFoam) TampinesSteamArray
description: Make TampinesSteamArray an all-Mach hybrid: keep the pressure-based PIMPLE skeleton, inject KNP central-upwind (rhoCentralFoam) dissipation as a Mach-weighted beta(Ma) deferred-correction flux. Copy the KNP flux MATH into tampines (NO outram-foam dependency; tampines already has all types + speed of sound w_ph_wood_wallis; preserve GPLv3/OpenFOAM provenance header). Opt-in SolverMode{Pimple,HybridAllMach}, default Pimple => beta=0 => bit-identical to current => plateau fix + 915 tests preserved by construction. Goal: damp the near-sonic ringing at the Edwards flashing front while retaining the plateau/no-subcooling.

notes.content: FIXED 2026-07-16. Root cause: not a physics limit of HEM but a numerical stiffness in the rarefied emptying tail. As the pipe empties past t~0.18s a cell rarefies in a localized runaway (rho 127->23->vacuum over ~350 steps); the conservative-EEqn diagonal rho_cont*V/dt collapses to its 1e-4 floor, the solve becomes ill-conditioned, and one step tips he from 951 kJ/kg to -7.3e6 kJ/kg -> below the 273.15K (p,h) edge -> panic. Both continuity and momentum KNP dissipation independently trigger it, so it is the explicit deferred correction being over-driven in the rarefied tail, not a sign error. Fix: rarefied-tail density taper on the KNP blend beta *= clamp((rho_face-50)/(100-50),0,1), rho_face=min(rho_o,rho_nb). Dissipation zero below 50 kg/m3 (rarefied -> pure PIMPLE, stable), full above 100. Measured min dissipated-face density over the 0-0.15s ringing window is 106.5 kg/m3, so the taper is inert there. Results: full 600ms HybridAllMach completes (no panic/NaN, void in [0,1]), plateau 387.7 psia, GS-1 RMSE 30.6 psia, no cold tail; 0-0.15s ringing -55.5% and plateau retained bit-identically; default Pimple bit-identical (920 lib tests pass). See collaboration/edwards_tampines_regen/hybrid_stability_debug_log.md + figures_hybrid_stable/. Not committed (maintainer commits).

title: Derive by hand: TampinesSteamArray discrete energy-conservation formulation (for paper methods)
description: By-hand analytical derivation of the conservative energy discretisation that fixed the Edwards blowdown plateau collapse (op-21g.14). Author's own derivation for the paper methods (Phase II row A of the Edwards debug timeline table, outram_park_th_paper/src/index.tex). Derive: (1) from the integral energy conservation law, the discrete conservative ddt (rho*h - rho_old*h_old)/dt, and show the h*div(rho u) term cancels against discrete continuity (the cancellation the non-conservative rho*dh/dt form breaks, dropping a term ~ h*(rho-rho_old)/dt that over-drains enthalpy during flashing); (2) why the storage density must be continuity-consistent rho_cont = rho_old - dt*div(phi), not the EOS density; (3) the effective compressibility psi = drho/dp|_h and why frozen isothermal kappa_T is ~100x too small in the two-phase dome (omits flashing term) -- this psi produces the flashing plateau.
acceptance_criteria: Self-contained written derivation of conservative ddt + rho_cont + psi=drho/dp|_h, ready for the paper methods section.

description: By-hand analytical derivation of the Mach-weighted KNP dissipation that removed the near-sonic ringing (op-21g.15). Author's own derivation for the paper methods (Phase II row B of the Edwards debug timeline table, index.tex). Derive: (1) the KNP (Kurganov-Noelle-Petrova) central-upwind numerical flux and its local wave speeds built from the HEM equilibrium sound speed, and how it enters PIMPLE as a deferred-correction flux; (2) the Mach-weight blending function beta(Ma) and the justification for gating on min(Ma) of the two adjacent cells rather than max(Ma) -- at a liquid/two-phase interface the liquid ~1400 m/s sound speed makes the KNP viscosity huge, but that wave is genuinely low-Mach and must not be dissipated, so min(Ma) activates KNP only where both sides are near-sonic; (3) why dissipation must act on static enthalpy rho*he, not total energy rho*E (carrying rho*E re-injects the -p pressure-work term and over-cools through 273.15K).
acceptance_criteria: Written derivation of KNP deferred-correction flux + beta(Ma) min-gating + static-enthalpy choice, ready for paper methods.

title: Velocity/Reynolds-dependent pipe-38 form loss to fix coupled DRACS low-flow cases (B1/C1)
description:
Follow-up to op-4wl.2/op-4wl.4 (pipe-38 K=0.8->17.8 SAM adoption, 2026-07-15). A single uniform form loss K=17.8 fixes the mid/high-flow DRACS over-prediction but cannot fix the two lowest-flow coupled cases B1 (655W) and C1 (841W), which already under-predict at K=0.8 and worsen to -6.62%/-6.80% under added resistance (form loss ~ v^2, negligible at low flow). They currently carry a documented per-point widened DRACS tolerance (B1 0.062->0.0676; C1 0.0676->0.069).

Proper fix: give pipe 38 a velocity/Reynolds-dependent loss of the form f_darcy = form_loss + b*Re^c, which is ALREADY supported by InsulatedFluidComponent::new_custom_component (see insulated_pipes_and_fluid_components/mod.rs:204, new_custom_component with reynolds_coefficient b and reynolds_power c). Shape needed: small a at low Re (helps B1/C1 low-flow under-prediction) rising to ~K=17.8-equivalent at high Re (preserves the mid/high-flow over-prediction fix). Calibrate b,c across all 25 coupled cases; re-validate the isolated-DRACS SAM reference (currently defined at constant K=17.8); then tighten B1/C1 tolerances back to the benchmark bound (0.062/0.0676) and recompute regression literals. Deferred from op-4wl.4 because per-iteration cost is a full ~50-min 25-case run and it would also require re-deriving the isolated SAM calibration.

title: basic-lib: SurfaceScalarField::uniform sets boundary face values to 0 (nulls fvm::laplacian boundary coeff)
description: Found during genfoam thermoMechanics mesh-solve port (op-p6p.11). outram-foam-basic-lib SurfaceScalarField::uniform() builds boundary patches via PatchField::zero_gradient(p.size), whose values are 0. Since scalar fvm::laplacian computes the boundary-face diffusion coeff as gamma.boundary[pi].values[fi]*area/d, a uniform gamma silently yields ZERO diffusion coefficient on every boundary face -> Dirichlet contributions dropped -> solve returns all-zeros yet reports converged (normalised_residual of x=0 with b=0 is 0). Workaround used in mesh_solve.rs: build the SurfaceScalarField with PatchField::fixed_value(size, k) boundary patches. Fix: SurfaceScalarField::uniform should set boundary values to the uniform value (fixed_value), or laplacian should treat a zero-gradient gamma patch as owner-extrapolated. Not my subtree; reporting per workspace rules.

title: offbeat: wire rheology into the mechanics solve (inelastic strain feedback, state advance, timestep control)
description:
P0 mechanics (op-6sl.1) and P1 rheology (op-6sl.2) are both ported and tested,
but nothing wires them together yet. MechanicsSolver still assumes pure linear
elasticity; ConstitutiveLaw::correct is never called.

The rheology port documents exactly what the mechanics layer must do
(rheology/mod.rs, "what the mechanics layer must do"):

1. Pass mechanical strain = total strain MINUS eigenstrain. Passing total strain
   makes an unconstrained, freely expanding pellet look highly stressed -- and it
   will then creep, which is silently and badly wrong.
2. Own one RheologyState per cell.
3. Call correct() repeatedly inside the outer corrector loop from the SAME
   start-of-step state; call advance() ONCE, after convergence. Advancing inside
   the loop double-counts inelastic strain.
4. The corrected stress is softer than the elastic one, so the displacement field
   is no longer in equilibrium -- re-solve with RheologyState::inelastic_strain()
   fed back as an additional eigenstrain (upstream's correctAdditionalStrain).
5. Bound the timestep with CreepTimeStepControl: the creep integration is
   implicit in stress but explicit in state.

Acceptance: a stress-relaxation case where a clamped bar under sustained strain
relaxes toward the creep-equilibrium stress, verified against the closed-form
exponential decay; and a case where free thermal expansion with creep active
produces NO creep strain (the eigenstrain-subtraction check in item 1).

Blocked by nothing -- both halves exist.

description: root@vm
title: root@vm
offbeat: mechanics must gate on MATPRO Zircaloy Poisson exceeding 0.5 above ~1355 K
description:
The ported MATPRO Zircaloy correlations fit Young's modulus and shear modulus as
independent lines, so nu = E/(2G) - 1 crosses the incompressible limit of 0.5 at
T = 1354.84 K and reaches 0.912 at 1800 K -- the top of upstream's own stated
validity range. At 600 K a retained cold-work fraction above 0.1197 does the same.

Consequence: lambda = E*nu/((1+nu)(1-2nu)) is singular at the crossover and
sign-flipped beyond it, and mechanics::LinearElastic::new rejects such constants
outright, so a hot-Zircaloy case will fail where upstream would silently produce
a garbage stiffness.

This is a faithful port of a real upstream defect, not a porting bug. Upstream
neither detects nor guards it.

PoissonRatioModel::is_admissible() was added for exactly this. The mechanics
layer needs to gate on it -- decide the policy: clamp below 0.5, fall back to a
constant Poisson's ratio, or refuse the case with a clear error. Maintainer call.

title: offbeat: deferred sub-models from the P3/P4 port (cracking, PyC anisotropy, PARFUME swelling, Lassmann burnup, relocation recovery)
description:
Deferrals recorded by the P3/P4 port agents, each documented in-file at the point
it applies. Collected here so they are not lost:

- Isotropic cracking (nCracks / sliceMapper / lhgr crack-softening) on the UO2,
  MOX and SCK-CEN Young's-modulus and UO2/MOX Poisson models. Needs damage-model
  state and a slice mapper, so not a pure function of MaterialState. All variants
  currently return the upstream nominal value.
- Transversely isotropic PyC: upstream itself returns the isotropic average
  (E_r + 2 E_t)/3 with a TODO. Real anisotropy needs a direction-dependent
  modulus in the mechanics layer.
- PARFUMEPyC thermal-expansion spherical-to-Cartesian tensor rotation: upstream
  does it in correct() using mesh_.C()[cellI]; it is a mesh operation and belongs
  in the mechanics assembly.
- swellingPARFUMEBuffer / swellingPARFUMEPyC: they integrate eps += rate*flux*dt,
  so they need fast flux and the timestep, plus a 2-D table interpolator in
  temperature x Bacon Anisotropy Factor and a 1-D one in coating density.
- burnupLassmann / burnupLassmannFBR (~75 KB): TUBRNP-style radial depletion
  solving a reduced Bateman chain for ~14 nuclides plus radial power
  reconstruction. That is neutronics and needs a flux solution.
- Axial-shape half of timeDependentAxialProfile: needs a mesh, pin direction and
  the profiles/ library.
- Relocation recovery (recoveryFraction/relaxRecovery), slice averaging, the
  max/min ratchets and the sensitivity scaling: history/mesh/contact logic.
- SCIANTIX physics: returns NotImplemented, never a silent zero. Separate
  MIT-licensed code with its own licence-provenance and V&V obligations.

Most of these are blocked on the same two things: the damage model and the
slice mapper. Worth sequencing them behind those rather than picking them off.

title: offbeat: source real literature validity ranges for correlations where the port chose its own

(273-1800 K), RelapZy (290-1800 K), MatproZy heat capacity (273-2099 K), IAEAZy
(273-2000 K), Banerjee (293-1273 K), SneadSiC (200-2400 K), Gehr (293 K cut-off),
IAEAZy density (1800 K), Zy emissivity (1500 K), Philipponneau (500 K lower
bound), HofmanD9, Tobbe, Watrous, and Lemehov's composition window.

Every other range in the port is a convention chosen by this crate, and each doc
comment says so explicitly rather than inventing a literature bound -- a test
asserts that no variant invents one.

Follow-up: source the real bounds from the literature (the oxide-fuel solidus
above all) and tighten them, replacing the port-chosen conventions. Until then
nobody should cite a range from this crate as a published limit.

title: outram-mc: root-cause the transport_csg stuck-history (MAX_EVENTS guard is a band-aid)
description: Before the MAX_EVENTS=100k/history cap, a reflective-infinite-medium k-eff hung (~9 CPU-min, one looping history). Find the geometry/nudge corner case (suspect: history stuck near a reflective plane/corner or coincident-surface re-cross in run_keff_csg) and fix properly; the cap currently leaks such histories (small bias).
closed_reason: Reflective-corner ping-pong fixed via compose_corner_reflection (retroreflection in one event); committed 69d8874. 3 regression tests + full suites green.

notes.content: Root-cause analysis (2026-07-24, from the op-6tz.34 work). The reflective-corner stuck-history is grazing-incidence ping-pong: a particle moving nearly parallel to a reflective wall, near a corner, alternately hits the two/three perpendicular walls at sub-nudge distances. Each fixed 1e-9 cm nudge advances it only ~1e-9 cm ALONG the wall, so traversing an O(1 cm) feature needs ~1e9 bounces >> MAX_EVENTS=100k -> the history is capped and leaked (the band-aid). This is distinct from op-6tz.34 (now fixed): that was a lattice-edge/wall coincident tie leaking histories OUT of the box; this is in-corner non-progress. A PROPER fix (per this bead: do NOT extend the band-aid) needs OpenMC-style token-based surface tracking (advance exactly to the surface, resolve the next cell by surface index + sense, and compose a corner reflection off all coincident reflective surfaces in one event) rather than a fixed position nudge. That is a larger rework best done against the OpenMC reference source (not available in this sandbox), so leaving open with this analysis. The residual ~2% surface-vs-delta gap in the op-6tz.34 regression test is plausibly this effect.
notes.author: root@vm

notes.content: Root-cause fixed: new Geometry::compose_corner_reflection in geometry.rs, called from cross_surface reflective arm. At a reflective corner/edge (other reflective walls within 1e-9 cm of the crossing point) it now reflects off ALL coincident walls in one event (reflections compose at a corner = retroreflection) instead of ping-ponging 1e-9 cm/event. Sign-agnostic crossing test so min-side corners handled; lone-wall case bit-identical. Marked honestly as a robustness fix for this crate's fixed-nudge tracker (no C++ ref on host). Regression tests in triso.rs. Measured: grazing history 100003 events + 20 corner leaks to 4 events + 0 leaks; small U235 reflective cube surface 2.22235+/-0.00334 vs delta 2.21925+/-0.00320 = 0.67 sigma. Suite green: 95 lib + 26 notebooks, 0 fail. CAVEAT: worktree based on main, 658 behind develop; develop-only nested-lattice ~2pct residual not measurable here. Verified fix ports cleanly to develop (cross_surface + triso imports identical). Not committed.
notes.author: root@vm

notes.content: Fixed in 69d8874 (integrated onto claude/outram-mc-setup-cb1bg9, which has op-6tz.34). Root cause: cross_surface reflective arm reflected a grazing near-corner particle off only the primary wall; the fixed 1e-9 cm nudge left it headed into the perpendicular wall(s), re-crossing at sub-nudge distances (~1e5-1e9 events → MAX_EVENTS leak, negative bias). Fix: Geometry::compose_corner_reflection composes the specular reflection of every reflective/white/periodic surface coincident with the crossing point (|evaluate(r)|<=1e-9) that the particle actually crosses (|u·n|>0, sign-agnostic for min/max-side axis-aligned walls). Retroreflection at a right-angle corner → particle leaves in one event. Lone-wall case is bit-identical to surf.reflect. MAX_EVENTS/NUDGE untouched. Tests: corner_reflection_composes_at_exact_corner (unit), corner_grazing_history_terminates_without_pingpong (worst 100003→4 events, 20→0 leaks), corner_reflective_cube_surface_tracking_unbiased (surface 2.22235±0.00334 vs delta 2.21925±0.00320, 0.67σ). 158 lib + 30 notebook tests pass; op-6tz.34 nested-lattice test still green. CAVEAT: robustness fix for this crate's fixed-nudge tracker (not an OpenMC routine port — only the physics is mirrored); non-orthogonal corners compose order-dependently (approximate), axis-aligned cube/lattice corners exact.

title: MSRE digital twin — offline demonstration (depletion + fission-product migration, real-time-capable)
description:
Offline demonstration digital twin of ORNL's Molten-Salt Reactor Experiment (MSRE, 1965-69) built on the OUTRAM PARK suite. Scope per RESPONSIBLE_USE.md: OFFLINE DEMONSTRATION / V&V / education only — no operational or live-plant coupling; MSRE is a public, decommissioned benchmark (ORNL-TM / ORNL-4xxx report series), so 'real time' means a real-time-capable simulation loop replaying/assimilating the historical record, not hardware monitoring. Data-policy clean (all MSRE data open literature).

Architecture: two-tier. OFFLINE high-fidelity (MC k-eig + depletion via outram-mc-libs+njoy; CFD via outram-foam; molten-salt Gibbs FP thermochemistry) generates reduced-order tables/models. REAL-TIME tier runs a circulating-fuel point-kinetics + 1-D loop TH (tuas/tampines, which already has FLiBe + HITEC salt correlations) + lumped Xe/FP-migration model in outram-park-digital-twin-engine (egui), with a state estimator (chem-eng real-time scaffolding) assimilating replayed MSRE data — which doubles as validation.

MSRE-specific hard physics: (1) circulating fuel => delayed-neutron precursors advect out of core (flow-dependent reactivity) - the defining effect; (2) Xe-135 gas stripping; (3) FP migration into three destinations (noble gases->off-gas, noble metals->plate on graphite/Hastelloy-N, salt-seekers->dissolved/precipitate) governed by salt redox (UF3/UF4).

Phasing: P0 zero-power circulating-fuel kinetics -> P1 add TH feedback -> P2 Xe+depletion -> P3 FP migration+chemistry -> P4 data assimilation. Each phase validates against a published MSRE dataset. All AI-assisted output is untrusted draft pending human V&V.

outram-foam-basic-lib: implement cyclic (periodic) patch support in the FV operators + matrix assembly
description: Port REAL cyclic-patch support into outram-foam-basic-lib. Investigation (2026-08-04): PatchKind::Cyclic is DECLARED (mesh/fv_mesh.rs:79 'Periodic / matching pair') and round-trips through polyMesh I/O (io/poly_mesh.rs:406/419 parse+write 'cyclic'), but is NOT wired into the FV operators or matrix assembly — grep finds Cyclic only in the enum decl, a doc comment, and the I/O string map; nothing in fvm::div / fvm::laplacian pairs cyclic faces or adds the across-boundary neighbour coupling. This is why the moltres MSR port (op-6w0.3) could not use it and fell back to a ring-of-internal-faces workaround. Deliverable: implement cyclic face-pairing (owner<->neighbour across the matching patch pair) in the FV discretisation so periodic domains work natively — required for a real 2-D/3-D MSR core coupled to a 1-D external loop. Scope: face-pair topology on Cyclic patch pairs, operator contributions (div/laplacian/interpolate) across the pair, matrix off-diagonal coupling, and a V&V case (e.g. 1-D advection/diffusion on a periodic ring matching the analytic periodic solution).

notes.content: Re-scoped per maintainer (2026-08-04). REMOVED the eigenvalue-acceleration item: the k-eigenvalue SOLVE already exists in the GeN-Foam port (outram-foam-appbuilder-lib/src/genfoam/neutronics/{diffusion,sp3,sn}/eigenvalue.rs — real outer power iteration + multi_region/outer_iteration.rs); it is NOT an outram-foam-basic-lib gap. Acceleration (Aitken/Chebyshev) is an optional enhancement to GeN-Foam's power iteration, tracked separately if wanted. Also: the moltres crate (op-6w0.3) duplicates a thinner eigenvalue solver and should eventually reuse GeN-Foam's neutronics rather than reinvent. This bead now scopes ONLY the confirmed real gap: functional cyclic-patch support in the FV operators. Robin/albedo BC is a minor separate item (GeN-Foam neutronics BCs unchecked).

title: Resume tutoring: rhoPimpleFoam momentum discretisation -> a_P u_P = H - grad(p) -> HbyA -> pressure equation
description:
TUTORING CHECKPOINT (one-step Socratic style per .claude/skills/tutor). Goal: teach the author rhoPimpleFoam's pressure-based algorithm from first principles, feeding (a) a new appendix section 'rhoPimpleFoam basic equations' and (b) understanding of op-26w Part 2 (compressibility psi = drho/dp|_h, why frozen isothermal kappa_T ~100x too small in the dome causes the plateau OVERSHOOT).

WHERE WE PAUSED: just wrote the continuous compressible momentum equation d(rho u)/dt + div(rho u u) = -grad(p) + div(mu grad u), labelled 4 terms (time, convection, pressure, viscous). Paused at the anchor question: identify the 3 'transport skeleton' terms (time+convection+viscous -> a_P, a_N, old-time) vs the 1 odd-one-out source (pressure).

NEXT STEPS (in order): (1) discretise momentum term-by-term into a_P u_P = H(u) - grad(p); (2) rearrange -> u_P = HbyA - rAU grad(p), with rAU=1/a_P, HbyA=H(u)/a_P (the code term that confused the author); (3) substitute the face velocity/flux into discrete continuity to BUILD the pressure equation (this closes the 'pressure is the orphan, continuity pins it' thread); (4) return to Part 2: compressibility psi and the plateau overshoot.

ALREADY COVERED & SOLID: Part 1 energy conservation fully derived by author (conservative vs non-conservative ddt differ by h*r; r=discrete continuity residual; rho_cont=rho_old-(dt/V)sum(phi.A) forces r=0). Author also patched the results-section discrete continuity eqn (added V_cell and face area vectors). FV diffusion stencil (rod example, a_P=a_E+a_W, Fick 2nd law) understood.

APPENDIX NOTE: 'rhoPimpleFoam basic equations' is textbook -- cite Jasak thesis, Ferziger & Peric, OpenFOAM programmer's guide; present as re-derived established background, NOT original, to keep novelty claims on the solver fixes.
acceptance_criteria: Author can derive a_P u_P = H - grad(p), HbyA, and the pressure equation unaided; appendix 'rhoPimpleFoam basic equations' drafted with textbook citations; then resume op-26w Part 2 (psi).

title: OpenFOAM upstream build not viable in remote container: background jobs reaped on idle
description:
Attempted to compile OpenFOAM Foundation dev (vendored at crates/outram-foam-turbulence-lib/upstream_source/OpenFOAM) in the Claude Code remote container, in order to run the incompressibleDriftFlux/dahl and multiphaseEuler/bubbleColumn coarse tutorials.

SETUP THAT WORKED: apt-installed flex + OpenMPI; built the wmake bootstrap tools (wmkdep, dirToString) via wmake/src/make; worked around the clone being named "OpenFOAM" while etc/bashrc expects "OpenFOAM-$WM_PROJECT_VERSION" by symlinking /opt/foam/OpenFOAM-dev to the vendored tree -- placed OUTSIDE the repo so build artifacts land in the gitignored dir and git status stays clean. Compilation itself is clean: zero real compile errors across ~1650 objects and 31 libraries.

BLOCKER: long-running background builds do not survive. Two launches died mid-build during idle gaps between turns (first ~35 min in, second ~8 min in). This is NOT resource exhaustion: no OOM entries, 14 GB RAM free, 19 GB disk free. setsid + nohup + detaching to PPID 1 did not help. Measured directly: a 9.3-minute FOREGROUND tool call advanced the build (objects 1618 to 1654, libs 28 to 31), while equivalent idle wall-clock advanced it by zero. Conclusion: the container only executes work while a tool call is active.

COST TO FINISH IN FOREGROUND: ~3800 of 5440 source files remain; at the observed rate in the current template-heavy stage that is roughly 4-16 hours of ACTIVE tool time (~25-100 dedicated 9.5-minute calls doing nothing but waiting). Not a sensible use of a session.

DIAGNOSTIC TRAP (cost an hour): pgrep -f make returns false positives because the claude process's own command line contains the word "make". Check liveness with: ps -eo pid,ppid,args | grep '[b]uild2.sh' and require PPID 1.

NOT BLOCKED, ALREADY DELIVERED (commit ce4bd82): the OUTRAM PARK equivalent V&V cases for all three targets, built from the upstream inputs verbatim, all passing -- GeN-Foam 1-D slab k_eff = 1.000008 vs analytical 1.000004 (0.4 pcm); dahl drift-flux settling 1.137e-3 m/s with the upstream simple closure reproduced exactly; bubbleColumn six-equation terminal slip 0.292 m/s with Schiller-Naumann drag.

SUGGESTED RESOLUTION: run the two OpenFOAM tutorials on a normal workstation and commit their reference output (mesh stats, alpha/U/T fields at the reported times) into the repo as stored benchmarks, so the Rust ports can be regression-compared without needing OpenFOAM in CI or in the container. Same pattern as the GeN-Foam/ESI bead.

description: Rename every crate that is a Rust translation/fork of an externally-trademarked open-source project to carry the outram-park-fork- prefix, so the name is unmistakably a fork and not the official project (see TRADEMARKS.md). Per-crate rename scope: (1) package name in the crate's Cargo.toml, (2) directory under crates/, (3) [workspace] members path in root Cargo.toml, (4) every path dependency on it in other crates' Cargo.toml, (5) every 'use <old_crate>::' / extern references in dependent crates + examples + tests, (6) publish metadata/README/docs mentions, (7) any CI / scripts referencing the path. crate:: self-references do NOT change (package-internal). title: fhr_sim_v2 reactor power oscillates after Nordheim-Fuchs kinetics swap (no delayed-neutron damping)
description:
User reports (2026-07-14): after replacing fhr_sim_v2's six-group SixGroupPRKE kinetics with teh-o-prke's Nordheim-Fuchs exact timestepper (op-dt3.7 / prke_backend/mod.rs), the reactor power oscillates a lot during operation. The old PRKE-based fhr_sim_v2 did not oscillate.

Likely root cause (physics, not a code bug): Nordheim-Fuchs is a PROMPT-only excursion model -- it neglects delayed-neutron precursor dynamics entirely (documented limitation in its module doc and the user-supplied design scaffold: 'Delayed-neutron-driven operational transients should remain in the PRKE subsystem'). The old six-group PRKE carried six delayed-neutron precursor groups whose decay constants act as a low-pass filter / inertia that damps the reactivity-power-temperature feedback loop. Nordheim-Fuchs has none of that damping, so the fuel-temperature feedback loop (alpha_f*(T-T_ref) -> power -> pebble-bed heating -> T) rings.

Contributing coupling detail in the fhr_sim_v2 wiring: each 1ms step, prke_backend overwrites nordheim_fuchs.fuel_temperature with the pebble-bed TH model's temperature (the authoritative, heat-removal-aware value), then steps NF. NF also advances T internally via its own adiabatic C_f dT/dt = P. The two temperature models can disagree step-to-step, feeding the oscillation.

Candidate fixes (not yet chosen -- discuss with user):
(a) Add the 'Delayed Neutron Layer' from the outram-park-dt-plan architecture (a precursor transfer-function bank, e.g. via chem-eng transfer functions) between the prompt-excursion layer and the TH layer, restoring delayed-neutron damping.
(b) Use Nordheim-Fuchs only for prompt-critical excursion DEMOS (its intended purpose) and keep six-group PRKE for quasi-steady operation in fhr_sim_v2 -- i.e. the NF swap may be the wrong model for this always-on operational sim.
(c) Relax/filter the pebble-bed->NF fuel-temperature hand-off and/or the reactivity feedback to damp the loop numerically (a band-aid, not physical).

Regression reference: git 86ccb04 (the NF swap) + 540fd45; the pre-swap PRKE version is the parent commit of 86ccb04's prke_backend.
closed_reason: Closed

notes.content: FIXED 2026-07-15 via option (a): added teh_o_prke::delayed_neutron_layer::DelayedNeutronLayer (5 first-order TransferFnFirstOrder lags) and wired it into fhr_sim_v2 prke_backend as a Lie-split point-kinetics update: NF advances the prompt part, the layer supplies the delayed source S=sum lambda_i C_i, total P = P_prompt + S*dt fed back to NF and to TH. Reconciled fuel-temp handoff: pebble bed is sole authoritative T owner; NF C_f aligned to pebble-bed heat capacity (8000kg*340). Headless regression (isolated kinetics+pebble-bed loop, dt=5ms, 80s, coolant fixed): prompt-only tail peak-to-peak = 194.2 MW on 31.8 MW mean (rings); with delayed layer = 0.0086 MW on 35.8 MW mean (22543x damping, settles). Regression tests added in both fhr_sim_v2 copies (engine canonical + tampines mirror): oscillation_regression::{delayed_neutron_layer_damps_power_oscillation, shipped_prke_timestep_settles}. Both fhr_sim_v2 copies build --release. beta_i/lambda_i from teh-o-prke six_group_constants U-235, reduced 6->5 groups (merged two fastest).

title: tampines components: physical size/volume representation for visualization
description:
Umbrella for giving tampines::components real physical dimensions.

FINDING (2026-08-03, while designing the digital-twin widget library): only Pipe carries real geometry (diameter, length, inclination, roughness -- crates/tampines/src/components/pipe.rs:37-43). HeatExchanger (heat_exchanger.rs:20) and SteamGenerator (via heat_exchanger.area) carry a heat-TRANSFER Area only, which is not an envelope -- a compact plate HX and a large shell-and-tube can share an area. Pump, Turbine, Valve, Condenser and CoolingTower carry no dimensional data at all.

WHY THIS BLOCKS THE WIDGET LIBRARY: outram-park-digital-twin-engine renders 'visual process objects whose rendering derives directly from physics state'. Its crate CLAUDE.md forbids new physics in the engine, so any dimension a widget needs must be added HERE, in tampines.

THE TRAP TO AVOID: HemSteamCv::get_volume() is reachable from Turbine (turbine.inlet) and SteamGenerator (secondary_side), but it is the THERMODYNAMIC control volume -- caller-supplied, unvalidated, used only to convert intensive to extensive properties (get_mass() = volume / specific_volume). The codebase convention is a 1 m3 dummy (TampinesSteamTableCV::get_ref_vol() returns exactly 1.0 m3) and Turbine::new never sets or scales it. Sizing a widget on it would draw every turbine identically at 1 m3. It represents the fluid parcel, not the machine casing. Do NOT use it for visual size.

Each child bead adds an honest envelope/size to one component. Prefer explicit named dimensions (casing length/diameter, shell height, footprint) over a bare Volume where the shape matters to the drawing; a single nominal Volume is acceptable where a rough size correlation is all that is wanted.

title: Nordheim-Fuchs exact timestepper -- prompt excursion + adiabatic fuel feedback
description:
Analytical (closed-form) integrator for prompt reactivity excursions with
adiabatic fuel-temperature feedback. Scaffolded from a design doc the user
supplied 2026-07-14 (Copilot-generated, pasted in chat). Purpose is NOT
reactor safety/licensing analysis -- it is an educational/visualization
model that removes prompt-lifetime stiffness (dt << Lambda) from real-time
sims, enabling interactive HTGR/fast-reactor demos on low-power devices
(Android tablets). Positioned as the "Prompt Excursion Layer" beneath the
existing delayed-neutron PRKE precursor-bank subsystem, which stays
untouched for delayed-neutron-dominated transients.

Physical model / assumptions:
- prompt neutrons only, delayed-precursor dynamics neglected
- lumped adiabatic fuel heat capacity C_f, uniform fuel temperature T_f
- fuel-temperature feedback only: rho_f = alpha_f * (T_f - T_f_ref)
- external reactivity rho_ext held constant over a timestep
- requires alpha_f < 0 (negative feedback) for a stable closed-form
  solution -- positive-feedback excursions are intentionally out of scope

Governing equations:
  dP/dt      = P * (rho_ext + alpha_f*(T_f - T_f_ref) - beta) / Lambda
  C_f dT_f/dt = P
where P = reactor power, T_f = lumped fuel temp, C_f = fuel heat capacity,
Lambda = prompt neutron generation time, beta = delayed neutron fraction,
rho_ext = externally imposed reactivity, alpha_f = fuel feedback coeff.

Reactivity-margin substitution r = rho_ext - beta + alpha_f*(T_f - T_f_ref)
collapses this to a Riccati-type ODE:
  dr/dt = (r^2 - gamma^2) / (2*Lambda)
  gamma^2 = r_k^2 + 2*Lambda*|alpha_f|*P_k/C_f   (real-valued since alpha_f<0)

Exact per-step update (closed form, no numerical ODE integration needed):
  r_{k+1}   = -gamma * tanh( gamma*dt/(2*Lambda) + atanh(-r_k/gamma) )
  T_f,{k+1} = T_f_ref + (r_{k+1} - rho_ext + beta) / alpha_f
  P_{k+1}   = C_f/(2*Lambda*|alpha_f|) * (gamma^2 - r_{k+1}^2)

This removes the dt << Lambda stability restriction a standard ODE stepper
would need, so timestep can be chosen for UI frame rate / TH-coupling
cadence / mobile performance instead of prompt-lifetime stiffness.

Explicitly OUT of scope for this model: delayed-neutron dynamics (stays in
the existing PRKE precursor-bank subsystem), licensing/safety-grade
calculations, reactor protection analysis, spatial kinetics, fuel-melt /
severe-accident modelling. It represents only the prompt self-limiting
mechanism via adiabatic fuel heating.

Deliverable here: the timestepper itself (struct + step function) living in
teh-o-prke, uom-typed per this crate's conventions, with a doc comment
carrying the methodology above (physical quantity / valid range / units,
per the root CLAUDE.md human-interface-layer rule -- alpha_f < 0 should be
a documented precondition, not silently assumed). Add a verification test
against a known Nordheim-Fuchs benchmark case once implemented (per this
workspace's V&V documentation rule: methodology + actual measured results
in the test's doc comment). nee_soon's consumption of this as its "Prompt
Excursion Layer" interface is a separate, dependent bead.

title: TransferFnFirstOrder response_vec growth in real-time loops (DelayedNeutronLayer / NF reactivity driver)
description: TransferFnFirstOrder (chem-eng) accumulates one FirstOrderResponse per input change and only clears after 20*tau. In DelayedNeutronLayer the slowest group (tau~80s) means the vector can grow to ~1.6M entries (20*80s at 1ms) before clearing in the always-on fhr_sim_v2 GUI loop, with O(n) per-step summation -> memory + slowdown over long real-time runs. Not a correctness issue (superposition is exact) and fine for the bounded headless regression tests (~seconds). Options: (a) add an exponential-integrator fast path to TransferFnFirstOrder / FirstOrderStableTransferFnNoZeroes that keeps O(1) state, or (b) periodic rebase of the lag to its current offset. Same concern applies to nordheim_fuchs's reactivity driver when the input changes every step. Surfaced during op-dt3.11.
closed_reason: Reimplemented DelayedNeutronLayer with direct implicit (backward-Euler) precursor time-stepping, replacing the 5 TransferFnFirstOrder lags whose response_vec grew unboundedly (O(n)/step). Per-group update C_i^{n+1}=(C_i^n+dt*(beta_i/Lambda)*P)/(1+dt*lambda_i), same discretisation as SixGroupPRKE's coefficient matrix but decoupled from the prompt equation (Nordheim-Fuchs owns prompt). Holds only 5 f64 precursor states -> O(1) time+memory, no growing Vec, no TransferFnFirstOrder. Public API unchanged (new/u235_five_group/advance/total_delayed_neutron_fraction/decay_constants/delayed_fractions/last_delayed_increment), so no consumer edits needed (fhr_sim_v2 in engine+tampines, htgr_sim_v1). VERIFIED: physics identical to old fix -- oscillation regression prompt-only 194.23 MW p2p -> delayed-layer 0.0086 MW (both fhr_sim_v2 copies); teh-o-prke 21 lib tests pass. PERF: new O(1) perf test (100k-step early vs late blocks after 20x more steps) -- late/early ratio 0.31, ~4-14 ns/step flat, vs old ~49us->1.8ms/step linear growth. Builds clean: teh-o-prke, engine fhr_sim_v2+htgr_sim_v1, tampines fhr_sim_v2. See op-dt3.11. Note under op-e46.

title: NF reactivity driver: same TransferFnFirstOrder response_vec growth in per-step loops
description: Follow-up split from op-e46.4 (DelayedNeutronLayer O(1) fix, done). teh-o-prke nordheim_fuchs::advance_with_reactivity_driver takes a &mut TransferFnFirstOrder and calls set_user_input_and_calc every step; if driven in an always-on real-time loop with a changing commanded reactivity it accumulates one FirstOrderResponse per input change (pruned only after 20*tau), i.e. the same O(n)/step + unbounded-memory growth op-e46.4 fixed in the delayed layer. NOT currently triggered in the shipped fhr_sim_v2 (prke_backend uses nordheim_fuchs.set_external_reactivity(...) directly, no TransferFn), so latent, not live. Options mirror op-e46.4: give the caller an O(1) exponential/implicit-integrator reactivity-lag path instead of a growing TransferFnFirstOrder, or periodically rebase the lag. Reference op-e46.4 / op-dt3.11.

MeshOp::Weld{distance} wired (infallible). 7 V&V tests pass in --release: exploded cube 24->8 chi=2, jittered soup, tol=0 no-op + exact-dup merge, non-transitive chain 3->1, degenerate-face drop, dispatch match. 114 lib tests, 0 warnings, doctests green. title: root@vm
outram-blender: fill holes (cap open boundary loops -> watertight)
description: Detect boundary loops (edges incident to exactly one face) and cap each with a centroid-fan triangulation, making an open surface watertight. Blender analogue: bmo_holes_fill / Fill Holes. Winding of each cap triangle is chosen opposite to the boundary directed edge so it stays consistent with the existing surface (adjacent faces traverse the shared edge in opposite directions). Directly serves the MC CSG bridge, which needs closed geometry. New MeshOp::FillHoles variant + dispatch. Pairs with weld (op-hzs.22): weld stitches near-coincident seams, fill-holes closes true gaps. closed_reason: Landed 2026-07-23 (commit 43c259c): src/fill_holes.rs caps open boundary loops with a centroid triangle fan. Boundary half-edge a->b = one whose reverse is absent; chained tail-to-head into loops; each loop capped with a centroid vertex + one [b,a,centroid] triangle per edge (reversed => winding stays consistent with the surface, no normals needed). Loops <3 edges left uncapped; fan documented as valid-not-minimal for non-planar holes. MeshOp::FillHoles wired (infallible). 4 V&V tests pass --release: open cube face -> V9 F9 E16 chi2 watertight (directed-half-edge uniqueness+reverse check); closed cube no-op; two-ended tube fills both -> V10 F12 chi2; dispatch match. 118 lib tests, 0 warnings, doctests green. description: Give a surface thickness: offset a copy of every vertex inward along its area-weighted vertex normal by 'thickness', add the inner shell with reversed winding (cavity-facing), and bridge open boundary edges with rim quads. Blender analogue: MOD_solidify (simple mode). Turns a surface patch into a volume (CFD wall meshing) or a closed mesh into a hollow shell. Reuses the boundary directed-edge tracing from fill_holes and consistent-winding rules. New MeshOp::Solidify { thickness } variant. V&V: open grid -> closed slab chi=2, watertight; closed cube -> nested outer+inner shells (hollow box) chi=4, each shell watertight; thickness=0 collapses inner onto outer.

Area-weighted vertex normals; outer shell keeps winding, inner shell = vertices offset inward by thickness with reversed remapped faces (cavity normals); open boundary edges bridged by rim quads [b,a,a+n,b+n] (winding-consistent). Open input -> closed slab, closed input -> hollow double shell. description: root@vm
title: root@vm
outram-blender: recalculate normals (make winding consistent + outward)
description: Blender's Recalculate Normals Outside (mesh.normals_make_consistent). BFS over face adjacency (shared undirected edges): flip any neighbour that traverses a shared edge in the SAME direction as its already-oriented neighbour, making each connected component consistently wound; then per component compute signed volume and flip the whole component if negative so normals point outward. Unlike boolean_general::orient_outward (which only whole-mesh-flips an ALREADY-consistent mesh by volume sign), this repairs an inconsistently-wound polygon soup -- foundational for boolean, the CSG inside-test, and solidify. New MeshOp::RecalculateNormals. V&V: a cube with a subset of faces reversed recovers full consistency + positive signed volume; an all-inward cube flips outward; an already-correct cube is unchanged.
closed_reason: Landed 2026-07-23 (commit 95fbeda): src/recalc_normals.rs makes winding globally consistent + outward. Adjacency by undirected edge; BFS orientation propagation (neighbour flip = orig_ab_g XOR !final_ab_f, directions compose by XOR); per-component signed-volume outward flip. Repairs inconsistent soup (unlike boolean_general::orient_outward which needs an already-consistent mesh). MeshOp::RecalculateNormals wired. 4 V&V tests --release: cube faces {0,2,4} reversed -> consistent, 6V=48>0 outward; all-inward cube flips outward; correct cube unchanged; dispatch match. 126 lib tests, 0 warnings, doctests green. Pure std+math -> Android-safe.

description: Blender's Bisect. Cut a mesh by a plane (point + normal) and keep the half where n.(x-point) <= 0, clipping every face against the half-space with Sutherland-Hodgman. New crossing vertices deduped per undirected original edge so adjacent faces share them. Leaves the cut open (composes with fill_holes to cap). Directly serves the CSG/MC half-space workflow. MeshOp::Bisect{point,normal} wired. 4 V&V tests --release: cube[-1,1]^3 bisected z=0(+z) -> open half, fill_holes -> watertight chi2 6V=24 (half of 8); plane outside keeps all; plane discarding all -> empty; dispatch match. 138 lib tests, 0 warnings, doctests green. outram-blender: read polyMesh (import) — round out polyMesh I/O
description:
outram-blender can already WRITE OpenFOAM polyMesh three ways (export::to_polymesh_text -> 5 ASCII strings; export::write_polymesh -> disk; feature-gated export::to_poly_mesh -> real outram_foam_basic_lib::io::poly_mesh::PolyMesh). It has NO reader, so a polyMesh cannot be loaded back into a Mesh. Add the import side to complete round-trip polyMesh I/O.

Recommended route (low-risk, no new parser): under the foam bridge feature, add export::from_poly_mesh(&outram_foam_basic_lib::io::poly_mesh::PolyMesh) -> Mesh that converts the PolyMesh points + faceList into the half-edge Mesh boundary surface (Mesh::from_polygons). Optionally also a feature-free ASCII parser (points/faces only) for standalone use without the foam dependency.

Caveats to document: a polyMesh is a VOLUME mesh (points/faces/owner/neighbour/cells); outram-blender's Mesh is a boundary surface, so import reconstructs the face soup (all faces), not cells. Winding/owner-neighbour orientation may need a recalc_normals pass.

V&V: round-trip a primitive — write_polymesh(cube) or to_poly_mesh(cube) -> from_poly_mesh -> assert V/E/F/chi == original cube (8/12/6/2), watertight after an optional recalc_normals. Methodology + measured results in the test doc comment per the workspace V&V rule.

With the foam crate's PolyMesh::read(dir) this imports an OpenFOAM constant/polyMesh dir; no new ASCII parser. Completes round-trip polyMesh I/O (write existed: to_polymesh_text/write_polymesh/to_poly_mesh). 2 V&V tests --release (foam-export): in-memory to_poly_mesh->from_poly_mesh 8/12/6/2 exact; on-disk write_polymesh->PolyMesh::read->from_poly_mesh 8/12/6/2 (real file read path). ARCHITECTURE DECISION PENDING: host in outram-blender (a new volume module set) vs a new sibling crate (e.g. outram-mesh-gen) that outram-blender drives. So the new outram-mesh-gen crate is confirmed: it CONSUMES an outram-blender surface Mesh, GENERATES tet->polyhedral cells (+prism layers), and EMITS a foam PolyMesh; foam's existing to_fv_mesh()/write() make it solvable/writable. title: cfmesh: octree near-wall refinement (hanging-node face splitting -> polyhedral cells)
description: Graded refinement: refine the carve's boundary-adjacent cells one level finer, keeping the mesh conforming by SPLITTING the coarse transition cell's face into the 4 fine sub-faces (hanging nodes) -> the coarse cell becomes polyhedral (>6 faces). v1: single-level near-boundary refinement (auto 2:1-balanced); multi-level + full balancing is future. Leaf model keyed by (level,i,j,k), points deduped by finest-resolution integer coord, emission rule 'finer side owns the split faces'. New octree module: refine_near_boundary(points,tris,base_cell_size). V&V: a box refined near its walls keeps EXACT box volume, validate() closed (incl polyhedral coarse cells), cell count grows, and some cell has >6 faces (a polyhedral transition cell).
closed_reason: Landed 2026-07-24: octree::refine_near_boundary — carve + one-level near-boundary refinement with HANGING-NODE face splitting (coarse transition face -> 4 fine sub-faces -> coarse cell becomes polyhedral >6 faces), mesh stays conforming. Leaves keyed (level,i,j,k); points deduped by finest int coord; each interface emitted once by finer side. v1 single-level (auto 2:1). 2 tests+doctest --release: box[0,4]^3 base 1 refined -> EXACT vol 64, validate closed (incl polyhedra), 456 cells (8+56*8), >6-face cells present. 22 tests, 0 warnings. description: root@vm

No hanging nodes (1:1 with wall faces). Needs a general assembler VolumeMesh::from_cell_faces (match shared faces by point-set) + cells_faces (invert owner/neighbour). New layers module: add_boundary_layers(mesh, patch, n, first_thickness, expansion). v1: a single closed wall patch. V&V: a box + N layers preserves EXACT volume (repartition), validate closed, cell count grows by N*n_wall_faces, the new outer wall sits at the original wall position, prism cells present.

V&V (3 tests, all green in release): exact volume preservation (repartition), validate() closed, cell count +n_layers*wall_faces, single-layer thickness honoured on flat-face column, n=0 no-op. Revisit only if internal solver code-reuse is specifically wanted.

title: Port CoolProp HumidAir (HAPropsSI) — uom + string APIs
description: Port HumidAirProp.cpp: virial coeffs (Baa/Caaa/Bww/Cwww/Baw/Caaw/Caww), enhancement factor f(T,p), psychrometric outputs (W, RH, wet-bulb, dew point, moist-air h/s/rho per kg dry air), inverse solves. Expose both a uom-typed HumidAir API and an HAPropsSI-style string function. Verify vs ASHRAE psychrometric points.

notes.content:
Scaffolded 2026-07-10 (src/humid_air/): mod.rs = HumidAirParam enum + HumidAirState + HumidAirError + ha_props(output,in1,in2,in3) (typed HAPropsSI) + solve_state dispatcher; virials.rs = B_aa/B_ww/B_aw + C_aaa/C_www/C_aaw/C_aww stubs; saturation.rs = p_ws/enhancement_factor/henry_constant stubs. All todo!(). Wired into lib.rs (pub mod humid_air), not in prelude. Builds; existing tests green.
IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-10 (not just scaffolded): humid_air module ported from CoolProp HumidAirProp.cpp -- virials (literal RP-1485 polynomial fits, B_aa/B_ww/C_aaa/C_www/B_aw/C_aaw/C_aww), enhancement factor secant solve, molar volume secant solve, ideal-gas enthalpy (simplified polynomial correlations). ha_props supports (T,p,W)/(T,p,R) input triples -> W/R/psi_w/H/V/p_w outputs. Verified vs ASHRAE psychrometric c_p/v to <0.1% (tests/humid_air_reference.rs). Found+fixed a real bug during verification: c_aaw was missing a /rhobarstar^2=1e6 factor (CoolProp source has TWO separate /1e6 divisions for that specific correlation, unlike its sibling c_aww), which had made the third-virial correction 4 orders of magnitude too large (5.5% V error before fix, <0.1% after). NOT implemented: entropy (needs CoolProp's ideal-gas reference-state offset calibration), wet-bulb/dew-point (need Brent solves). Remains open for those.
Wet-bulb + dew-point IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-13 (entropy remains open).

dew_point_temperature: ported CoolProp's DewpointTemperature secant solve
almost verbatim, seeded via this crate's own vle::saturation_temperature
(IAPWS-95) in place of IF97 Tsat97. Verified: T=30C/RH=50% -> Tdp=18.451C
(matches the well-known ~18.4C psychrometric-chart value).

wet_bulb_temperature: ported CoolProp's WetBulbSolver energy-balance
residual (LHS-RHS), root-found by bisection on [T_dp, T] instead of
CoolProp's Brent-with-fallback-bracket logic -- T_wb always lies in
[T_dp, T] (standard psychrometric fact), which sidesteps needing
CoolProp's own T_sat-adjacent bracket-clamping special case entirely
(its upstream comments cite real historical bugs #2255/#2690 about that).

Caught and fixed a real bug during verification: the first implementation
evaluated liquid water's enthalpy via flash::state_pt, which only reaches
the vapour/supercritical branch (documented in its own doc comment) --
wrong branch for the subcooled liquid water present at a typical T_wb. It
silently returned a nonsense enthalpy (~-4.2e22 J/kg for liquid water at
20C/1atm) instead of erroring. Fixed by using the saturated-liquid density
at T_wb (vle::saturation_at_temperature) instead, since liquid enthalpy is
only weakly pressure-dependent -- reuses the same pattern
saturation::vbar_ws already relies on elsewhere in this module.

Verified in tests/humid_air_reference.rs: (1) exact saturation identity
T_dp=T_wb=T at R=1 (rigorous, not approximate); (2) cross-check against
Stull (2011) J.Appl.Meteor.Climatol. 50:2267-2269's independent empirical
wet-bulb formula, <0.5C (30C/50%RH: 22.00C vs Stull 22.30C; 25C/60%RH:
19.47C vs Stull 19.50C). All 6 tests in that file pass; full crate suite
(240+ tests across all files) still passes; docs/api.md regenerated.

Remaining: entropy S still needs the ideal-gas reference-state offset
calibration (separate porting effort); T_wb/T_dp still output-only, not
yet supported as input keys.
Entropy S + T_wb/T_dp as input keys IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-13.

T_wb/T_dp as inputs: psi_w_from_dew_point (exact, non-iterative -- the dew
point IS the definition) and psi_w_from_wet_bulb (bisection parameterised
by trial dew point, reusing the already-verified forward wet_bulb_temperature
as the inner black-box). Needed a targeted fix for the exact-saturation
edge case (T_wb=T at R=1): the general bisection bracket degenerates there,
and the forward solve's own secant noise (~1e-7 K) can land T_wb on either
side of T, tripping an over-tight 1e-9 K bounds check. Fixed with a direct
psi_w = psi_ws(T,p) short-circuit + loosened bounds tolerance to 1e-4 K.
Verified via round-trip (T,p,R)->T_dp/T_wb->(T,p,T_dp/T_wb)->R, <1e-4,
including the R=1 edge case.

Entropy: NOT a port of CoolProp's own ensure_ref_offsets/calc_ideal_gas_alpha0
machinery (which needs the real ideal-gas Helmholtz term + a historical
multi-point calibration) -- CoolProp's own C++ literally prints "Not
implemented" for entropy in the simplified-polynomial-enthalpy branch this
crate already uses for H, so there's no CoolProp reference implementation
to port in this configuration at all. Instead: derived via Gibbs' theorem
(pure-component ideal-gas entropies at the mixture's total T,p, Cp(T) from
the SAME polynomials already verified for H) + the standard virial/mixing
corrections, anchored to an explicit ASHRAE zero-point convention (dry air
S=0 at 0C/1atm; water's constant derived via Clausius-Clapeyron from H's
own existing 0C anchor, confirmed consistent: h_w(0C)=2501 kJ/kg matches
the known latent heat of vaporization to 3 figures, now a permanent unit
test in mod.rs).

Caught a real bug during verification: first version used dry air's own
virial-corrected molar volume (+R*ln(v_a/v_a0)) mirroring CoolProp's own
volume-based formula -- but CoolProp's version evaluates the REAL ideal-gas
Helmholtz term there (density-native), while this port integrates Cp (the
CONSTANT-PRESSURE heat capacity), so the volume form silently smuggled in
a second, spurious T-dependence (v_a is proportional to T at fixed p),
breaking dS/dT=Cp/T by ~28% at 25C. Fixed by using -R*ln(p/p0) (total
pressure, Gibbs' theorem) for both air and water instead.

Verified: dS/dT=Cp/T (rigorous, model-independent thermodynamic identity)
holds to 7e-4 to 1.2e-3 across T=1-40C, W=0-0.02 kg/kg -- small, smooth,
and of the same order as the virial correction's own size (consistent with
a residual virial-cross-term path-dependence artifact, not a remaining bug).
CAVEAT, documented in the module doc: S's absolute value is NOT verified
against CoolProp or an external table (different reference-state convention
than CoolProp's own, and H's own mixture value already has a known ~6.6
kJ/kg ASHRAE offset that S likely inherits) -- only the temperature
dependence is rigorously verified. Full crate suite (241+ lib tests, 10 in
humid_air_reference.rs) passes; docs/api.md regenerated.

Remaining open in this bead: absolute-value cross-check for S against a
real external reference, if/when op-kbc.3 (rfluids oracle) lands.

title: Extend OPCPFluidArray with TUAS-FluidArray-like interface (lateral coupling, heat source, geometry, flow bookkeeping)
description:
Give OPCPFluidArray (rhoPimpleFoam/mod.rs) a subset of tuas_boussinesq_solver's
FluidArray interface, so a future TAMPINES Pipe component can enum-dispatch
between a TUAS backend and a coolprop backend interchangeably. Scope
(confirmed with user via plan-mode session 2026-07-13, see
outram-park-dt-plan.md at workspace root and the full planning-tool record):

- New fields: lateral_adjacent_array_temperature_vector/conductance_vector
  (Vec<Vec<T>>, not Array1 -- coolprop has no ndarray dep), q_vector/
  q_fraction_vector (heat source), wetted_perimeter, incline_angle,
  mass_flowrate, pressure_loss, internal_pressure_source.
- Simplified vs TUAS: no NusseltCorrelation or DimensionlessDarcyLossCorrelations
  port -- caller supplies conductance/pressure-loss values directly.
- Lateral coupling + heat source wired into step()'s energy equation now
  (one-line addition to the existing explicit source-term loop, alongside
  conv_he/dp_dt). Geometry/flow-bookkeeping fields stay pure bookkeeping,
  not read by step() (matches TUAS itself).
- New error type OPCPFluidArrayError::LengthMismatch (own type, not a
  MeshError reuse), properly re-exported from lib.rs (fixes the existing
  MeshError-not-exported gap in the same pass).
- New file rhoPimpleFoam/lateral_coupling.rs (mirrors TUAS's own
  directory-per-concern split for this exact feature) -- 13 new methods,
  7 new tests.
- set_temperature_vector needs a real per-cell (p,T) flash + write
  he/rho/t/psi together, NOT a plain t field write (he is the actual PIMPLE
  state variable; a plain t write would be silently undone by the next
  correct_thermo() call).

This is Part 1 of a 3-part plan (Part 2: new tampines crate, Part 3: new
outram-park-digital-twin-gui crate) -- this bead covers Part 1 only.

notes.content: Done 2026-07-13: lateral_coupling.rs created (13 methods, 7 tests), new() field initializers added, step() wires lateral conductance + heat source into the energy-equation source term (extensive Watts, matching conv_he/dp_dt units), clear_vectors() called at end of step(). OPCPFluidArrayError re-exported from lib.rs. Test fix: test fluid changed from Water (liquid at 300K/1bar -- unreachable by the vapor-branch flash, silently no-ops every correct_thermo/state_pt call) to Nitrogen (matches existing passing tests' fluid choice). Also found t/rho lag he by one outer-corrector iteration in this PIMPLE solver -- tests call correct_thermo() after step() to sync t before reading temperature. Tutor: rhoPimpleFoam stability issues (teaching doc for OutramFoam/tampines)
description: User wants a step-by-step, teacher-to-student explanation of the rhoPimpleFoam pressure-velocity stability issues discovered 2026-07-14, written as durable documentation in the OutramFoam rhoPimpleFoam solver folder (crates/outram-foam-appbuilder-lib/src/solvers/rho_pimple_foam/), and referenced from tampines docs. Should walk through, pedagogically: (1) why compressible PISO couples p and U and how the pEqn is assembled from the momentum diagonal (rAU) + laplacian + psi*V/dt compressibility term; (2) the pressure-source clobbering bug -- fvm::laplacian puts the FixedValue-pressure Dirichlet source (coeff*p_bc) into the matrix source, and overwriting it (p_eqn.source = ...) kept the diagonal but dropped the source, silently imposing p_bc=0 and blowing up any fixed-pressure outlet even from equilibrium; the fix is to ADD not overwrite; (3) the phi_hbya boundary write-back for FixedValue velocity patches; (4) stiff-liquid water-hammer: near-incompressible liquid + impulsive inlet -> Joukowsky surge rho*c*du, reflection undershoots to negative absolute pressure -> out of EOS range; why gas (large psi) is well-conditioned but liquid (tiny psi) is stiff; (5) the standard fixes -- OpenFOAM pressureControl pMin/pMax bounding (limit pressure not density for complex EOS), PISO vs SIMPLE vs PIMPLE and under-relaxation, acoustic CFL dt<dx/c, and velocity ramping; (6) BC well-posedness (fixed-velocity inlet + fixed-pressure outlet, inletOutlet for backflow). Cite the OpenFOAM pressureControl source and the rhoSimpleFoam complex-EOS commit. This is the durable pedagogical companion to bead op-21g.12.

title: genfoam multiRegion: per-cell / dynamic mesh XS feedback (neutronics-subtree API gap)
description: MeshNeutronics (multi_region/mesh_region.rs) currently drives DiffusionNeutronics with a GLOBAL Doppler feedback: it collapses the mapped TFuel field to one importance-weighted mean temperature and re-materialises the whole-mesh cross sections at that single point (DiffusionXsFields::materialize takes one feedback vector for all cells). Two neutronics-subtree API additions would lift this to full fidelity: (1) a materialize variant accepting a PER-CELL parameter array so each cell's XS use its local temperature (upstream setNeutronicsVariables.H evaluates per cell); (2) a public DiffusionNeutronics::set_k_eff / dynamic-reactivity setter so a scalar Delta-rho from the ReactivityFeedback layer can be injected into a diffusion TRANSIENT step (step() currently reads k_eff only from solve_eigenvalue; there is no public mutator, so the mesh path demonstrates negative feedback via steady eigenvalue re-solves, not a dynamic transient reactivity insertion). Both are edits to crate::genfoam::neutronics (owned by the neutronics fleet), out of scope for the multi_region subtree. Until then the global-feedback + steady path is real and closes the loop (V&V in mesh_region.rs tests).

title: Pipe transient (dynamic) Brent-based cell-network solver
description: DWSIM Pipe.vb's RunDynamicModel: represents a pipe as a chain of accumulation-stream cells, solves inter-cell mass flow via Brent root-find on the pressure-difference residual per timestep (compressible, volume-conserving). Deferred -- op-qo2.1 only ports the steady-state correlations (Beggs-Brill/Lockhart-Martinelli/Darcy-Weisbach); tampines' own single_phase (TUAS FluidArray) / compressible (OPCPFluidArray) wrappers already provide transient pipe behavior for their respective backends.
closed_reason: Ported from DWSIM Pipe.vb's RunDynamicModel(): src/pipe/transient.rs -- PipeCell (fixed-volume mass-balance accumulator, density = mass/volume, advance_mass_balance() over a timestep) and solve_intercell_mass_flow() (Brent root-find on the pressure-drop residual, DWSIM's Pdrop_transition - dpt(mass_flow) = 0). Used the roots crate's existing Brent implementation (BSD-2-Clause, already an approved workspace dependency, not yet used elsewhere) rather than hand-rolling one, since Brent's method itself is standard numerical-methods machinery, not DWSIM-specific -- added roots.workspace = true to this crate's Cargo.toml. DWSIM's IPOPT least-squares fallback (when Brent fails to converge) was not replicated -- Brent's own SearchError is surfaced directly instead, and this crate has no IPOPT-equivalent solver to reach for regardless. The (V,T)->P flash DWSIM does per cell after each mass transfer is explicitly left to the caller (same flash-dependency pattern as heat_exchanger/expander/pump). 4 new tests (46 total, 0 warnings): forward-flow and reverse-flow root-finding against a linear resistance model, and PipeCell mass-balance/density sanity checks. cargo build/test --release and cargo doc (deny broken-intra-doc-links) both pass clean.

title: basic-lib: add traction (sigma.n=0) BC on D and anisotropic (tensor-coeff) laplacian for thermo-mechanics
description: Follow-ups surfaced by genfoam thermoMechanics mesh solve (op-p6p.11). (1) fvm::laplacian_vec only takes a scalar coefficient (2mu+lambda); an anisotropic stiffness needs a tensor-coefficient laplacian operator. (2) The field boundary layer offers only Dirichlet (FixedValue) and zero-gradient on D; a traction boundary condition (sigma.n = given, e.g. stress-free surface under thermal load where dD/dn != 0) is not expressible, so the stress-free free-thermal-expansion case can only be reached via a non-uniform temperature with Dirichlet ends. (3) fvc::grad_vec sets a zero-gradient output boundary, so the compact-normal-stress divSigmaExp correction carries no boundary-gradient info (exact on 1-D columns, approximate near 2-D/3-D boundaries). (4) No non-orthogonal gradient correction. See src/genfoam/thermo_mechanics/mesh_solve.rs limitations note.

title: GeN-Foam build blocked in container: ESI OpenFOAM v2506 unreachable
description:
GeN-Foam (gitlab.com/foam-for-nuclear/GeN-Foam, cloned OK to /opt/foam/GeN-Foam) declares in its README that it is built on the OpenFOAM ESI/OpenCFD distribution, currently v2506 (openfoam.com) — NOT the OpenFOAM Foundation 'dev' distribution (openfoam.org) that this repo vendors at crates/outram-foam-turbulence-lib/upstream_source/OpenFOAM. The two distributions are API-incompatible for a solver as deeply integrated as GeN-Foam.

Blocker: the remote-execution container's network policy denies both dl.openfoam.com and develop.openfoam.com (agent proxy returns 403 to CONNECT). github.com and gitlab.com ARE reachable. There is no official ESI mirror on those hosts, and pulling an unofficial third-party mirror was deliberately NOT done — provenance/licence review is required per RESEARCH_INTEGRITY_AND_PROVENANCE.md, so an unverified mirror is not acceptable for this project.

Consequence: GeN-Foam cannot be compiled or run in this container. This is an environment constraint, not a code defect.

What WAS delivered instead (commit ce4bd82): the OUTRAM PARK equivalent V&V case for GeN-Foam's Tutorials/guidedCases/1_reactorSlab_1D_1Gr_neutronicDiffusion, built from that tutorial's nuclearData verbatim (D=0.1275, sigmaRemoval=5.0082, nuSigmaEff=5.5675, P0 scatter 0.1, IV, 6-group beta/lambda) on a 151-cell 1.5 m slab. It verifies against the closed-form one-group bare-slab solution: k_eff = 1.000008 vs analytical 1.000004 (0.4 pcm), and reproduces the k_inf = 1.111677 quoted in the upstream README — confirming the in-group-scattering convention matches.

To unblock: either (a) allowlist dl.openfoam.com / develop.openfoam.com for this environment, or (b) build on a machine with ESI OpenFOAM v2506 already installed, or (c) run the GeN-Foam tutorial elsewhere and commit its reference output as a stored benchmark for regression comparison.

description: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
title: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
Haverkamp (1977) constitutive model + kr(pc) interface
description: The Celia 1990 problem uses Haverkamp et al. (1977) relations where relative permeability is a function of pressure head psi, not saturation: theta(psi)=theta_r+alpha(theta_s-theta_r)/(alpha+|psi|^beta); K(psi)=Ks*A/(A+|psi|^gamma). CharacteristicCurves currently exposes relative_permeability(Se) which cannot represent K(psi). Add a Haverkamp variant and widen the curve interface so k_r can be evaluated from capillary pressure directly (analytic dkr/dpc, FD-checked). Head<->pressure convention psi=-pc/(rho g), cm vs Pa. Depends on op-v6s.7.

notes.content: Implemented 2026-07-22 (branch claude/pflortran-merge-develop): Haverkamp variant added to CharacteristicCurves with celia_1977_sand() preset, analytic FD-checked derivatives, and an end-to-end RICHARDS integration test. NOTE / deviation from the bead text: the curve interface was NOT widened for kr(pc) directly -- kr fits the existing kr(Se) interface exactly via the Se<->|psi| bijection, so widening proved unnecessary. REMAINING before close: wire Haverkamp into the io deck parser (needs the extra params alpha/beta/A/gamma/theta_r/theta_s), which is really op-v6s.9.2 scope. Verification-only; human V&V sign-off still pending.

title: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
v1 GUI clobbers shared state with a stale full-struct overwrite (lost-update race)
description:
Found 2026-07-28 while porting to v2. v1's GUI does: clone CIETState early in the egui repaint, mutate a couple of control fields on the clone, then overwrite_state(clone) at the end -- a full-struct store from a stale snapshot, ~20x/second. Sites: examples/ciet_educational_simulator/ciet_simulator_v1/app/panels_and_pages/main_page.rs:109 and :1194, and the frequency-response block in app.rs.

Impact in v1: mild and self-healing. CIETState is a publication surface, not the solver's internal state -- the physics thread recomputes temperatures from its own tuas component objects each timestep, so clobbered OUTPUTS are restored within one step. That is presumably why this was never noticed.

Impact in v2: NOT benign. CIETState also carries the CONTROLS the solver reads each timestep (heater power, pump pressure, set points). With OPC-UA writes arriving from remote clients at arbitrary times, a client write landing between the GUI's clone and its store is silently discarded -- remote control would appear to randomly not take effect, and would be near-impossible to diagnose from the client side.

Fixed in v2 by writing only the specific fields the GUI actually changed, under a short write guard, instead of overwriting the whole struct (main_page.rs:134 and :1236).

Consequence for port equivalence (op-wqk.13.6): v1 and v2 will NOT agree step-for-step with a GUI running, because v1 discards updates and v2 does not. The comparison must therefore be run HEADLESS on both sides to be meaningful.

No fix proposed for v1 itself -- out of scope for the v2 request, and v1 is the maintainer-validated reference. Flagging for his decision.

title: Tensor/vector FV operators for GeN-Foam thermoMechanics (unblocks op-p6p.11)
description:
Additive, non-breaking tensor/vector-field FV operators translated from vendored OpenFOAM (commit 481094fd), flagged blocking by the GeN-Foam thermo-mechanics port (op-p6p.11):

1. fvc::grad_vec: VolVectorField -> VolTensorField (Gauss grad, outer(Sf,u_f))
2. fvc::div_tensor: VolTensorField -> VolVectorField; fvc::div_symm_tensor: VolSymmTensorField -> VolVectorField (Gauss div, Sf & sigma_f)
3. fvm::d2dt2: implicit Euler 2nd time-derivative for VolVectorField -> FvVectorMatrix
4. fvm::Sp / fvm::Su / fvm::su_sp: implicit + explicit source terms (scalar & vector)
5. Field-level tensor algebra: tr/symm/two_symm/dev/dev2 on VolTensorField/VolSymmTensorField

Translated from src/finiteVolume/finiteVolume/{fvc/fvcGrad,fvc/fvcDiv,fvm/fvmSup,fvm/fvmD2dt2} + gaussGrad/gaussDivScheme/EulerD2dt2Scheme. V&V tests: grad(A.x)=A^T, div(linear tensor)=known const, d2dt2(quadratic-in-t)=const. Unblocks op-p6p.11 (deferred GeN-Foam thermoMechanics/TH mesh solves).
closed_reason: Tensor/vector FV operators implemented, V&V tested (13 tests pass), Android+clippy clean, additive/non-breaking. Unblocks op-p6p.11.

notes.content:
DONE 2026-07-15. Added (all additive, non-breaking):
fvc::grad_vec (VolVectorField->VolTensorField, gaussGrad outer(Sf,u_f)); fvc::div_tensor + fvc::div_symm_tensor (Vol[Symm]TensorField->VolVectorField, gaussDivScheme Sf&sigma); fvm::d2dt2 + d2dt2_coeff (VolVectorField ->FvVectorMatrix, EulerD2dt2Scheme, constant-dt); fvm::{sp,su,su_sp,sp_vec,su_vec,su_sp_vec} (fvmSup, OpenFOAM signs: Sp diag+=V*sp, Su source-=V*su); fields::vol_field_algebra::{tr,tr_of_symm,symm,two_symm,two_symm_of_symm,dev,dev2,dev_of_symm,dev2_of_symm}. Added PatchField::{zero_gradient_tensor,fixed_value_tensor,zero_gradient_symm_tensor,fixed_value_symm_tensor}. 13 new V&V tests, all pass (grad(A.x)=A^T; div(linear tensor)=x-row of M; d2dt2(quadratic-in-t)=2c; Sp/Su solve k.phi=S). cargo test -p outram-foam-basic-lib --lib --release: 245 passed 0 failed 4 ignored. Android aarch64-linux-android check clean. clippy clean on new files. No existing public signatures changed. Unblocks op-p6p.11 (GeN-Foam thermoMechanics DEqn/TEqn). Follow-up for op-p6p.11: no fvm::laplacian(tensor-coeff) or explicit non-orthogonal correction; grad_vec is single Gauss pass; d2dt2 assumes constant dt + non-moving mesh (no V0/V00 history in FvMesh).

description: root@vm
title: root@vm
cfmesh: boundary layers on curved / polyhedral walls (snappyHexMesh-style layer addition)
description: add_boundary_layers is V&V'd + reliable on FLAT (box) walls but invalidates the mesh on CURVED walls (snapped sphere/cylinder) and on polygonal (dual) wall faces — the averaged inward-normal extrusion self-intersects / inverts on convex curvature. Mesh Studio currently gracefully SKIPS layers there (falls back to the valid polyhedral dual) and reports it. Needed for real curved-geometry CFD near-wall resolution: per-point feature-aware normals, layer-thickness limiting by local cell size, layer collapse/termination where cells would invert (snappyHexMesh addLayers strategy). V&V: sphere/cylinder + N layers -> valid + solvable, prism cells present at the wall, volume conserved. Blocks the full 'polyhedral mesh with layers' story for curved reactors in Mesh Studio (examples/mesh_studio).

notes.content: Curved-wall layers working (commit a52636a): add_boundary_layers_adaptive — smoothed normal field (Laplacian passes over wall-point adjacency) + per-point thickness cap (fraction of local wall spacing) + global validity back-off (scale down until closed). Diagnosis: min-faces dual + THIN layers was already valid on the sphere; failure was thickness-driven self-intersection, not topology — back-off targets that. Mesh Studio now inserts real prism layers on sphere (6583 cells) + cylinder (3978), valid, 0 inverted, volume conserved. BL non-orthogonality ~79-81deg is expected (>checkMesh 70deg warning, handled by non-orthogonal correctors) — GUI explains this. V&V: 3 tests (sphere/cylinder/box). REMAINING (keep open): back-off is GLOBAL (one tight feature thins whole wall); true per-point LOCAL layer termination + height-by-feature-size (snappyHexMesh addLayers / AFLR advancing-layer) still to do for optimal thickness on mixed-curvature geometry.
